correctness.rationale: PASS: For reflected Brownian generator D d²/dx² with occupation local time D/epsilon integral, the inverse-local-time transform at threshold ell is exp[-(R+ell)sqrt(s/D)]. A Poisson cycle of rate r has positive local-time reward Y with probability a=exp(-R sqrt(r/D)), conditional Y exponential rate k=sqrt(r/D). Hence E Y=a/k and long-run production J=r a/k=sqrt(Dr) exp(-R sqrt(r/D)). Poisson count bounds plus exponential moment of iid Y give exponentially small deviations of L_t/t from J without assuming cycle duration/reward independence. For independent regular-varying threshold Psi in RV_-alpha, squeeze E Psi(L_t) at (J±delta)t and Karamata yield survival ~Psi(Jt); for Lomax mean iff alpha>1. Freshly redrawing both progress and threshold produces geometric independent attempts p=exp(-Rk) E exp(-k Lambda)>0; renewal transform has a moment-generating function for small positive argument, hence exponential tail. Reviewed CHECK.py only supplies finite integral checks; proofs handle infinite time.

value.rationale: PASS: In a natural encounter-based reaction model, two reset conventions differing only in whether the hidden threshold is redrawn lead to different tail *classes* (power versus exponential) and different moment finiteness despite common spatial reset dynamics. An exact survival equivalence with prefactor J is needed to classify heavy-tailed reaction time; not merely recomputation of the preknown optimization of J or a tiny numerical instance.

limitations: One-dimensional normal reflected diffusion, r,D,R>0, fixed independent random threshold continuous with regular variation, fresh redraw on each reset; Lomax alpha=1 criterion not universal for arbitrary slowly varying factors.
